subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Magellan's Deadly Circumnavigation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Magellan's Deadly Circumnavigation.

hook.text: Magellan proposed sailing around the entire Earth. The Spanish king funded it. Magellan died halfway through.

buildup.text: The fleet of five ships left Spain in 1519. Mutinies, starvation, and scurvy plagued the journey from the start.

discovery.text: Only one ship and 18 of the original 270 crew returned. The voyage proved the Earth was round and vast.

twist.text: Magellan was killed in the Philippines in a battle he chose to fight for prestige rather than strategy.

climax.text: Magellan committed to an irreversible path. Once you are mid-ocean, turning back is as dangerous as pressing forward.

punchline.text: No turning back mid-ocean. Commitment can trap you as much as save you.

quiz.question: What decision trap does Magellan's voyage illustrate?
options: Irreversible commitment where turning back is as risky as continuing
